slides.title: 3 books that actually fix procrastination
slides.body: (not motivation. systems.)

slides.title: Eat That Frog
slides.body:
Brian Tracy

Do your hardest, most important task first thing. Everything after it feels easy.

slides.title: Atomic Habits
slides.body:
James Clear

The two-minute rule: shrink the habit until it takes 2 minutes. "Study" becomes "open the notes." Starting is the hard part.

slides.title: The 5 Second Rule
slides.body:
Mel Robbins

When you hesitate, count 5-4-3-2-1 and move before your brain talks you out of it.

slides.title: Try one tomorrow morning.

slides.title: 4 money books to read before you turn 20
The Psychology of Money
slides.body:
Morgan Housel

Getting rich and staying rich are different skills. Behaviour beats intelligence.

slides.title: I Will Teach You to Be Rich
slides.body:
Ramit Sethi

Automate saving and investing so it happens without willpower. Spend guilt-free on what you love, cut the rest.

slides.title: Rich Dad Poor Dad
slides.body:
Robert Kiyosaki

Assets put money in your pocket. Liabilities take it out. Know which one you're buying.

slides.title: The Millionaire Next Door
slides.body:
Thomas Stanley & William Danko

Many millionaires look ordinary. Looking rich and being rich are often opposites.

slides.title: Start with #1.

posts.caption: The most important lesson in The Psychology of Money. #booktok #investing #compounding

slides.title: The lesson from The Psychology of Money that changed how I think about time
Warren Buffett is one of the richest people alive.
slides.body: But according to Morgan Housel, the vast majority of his wealth came after his 65th birthday.

slides.title: His secret wasn't just skill.
slides.body: It was time. He started investing as a kid and never stopped.

slides.title: Compounding rewards patience, not genius.
slides.body: Small amounts, left alone for decades, beat big amounts started late.

slides.title: So the best time to start is now.
slides.body: Even $10. Even at 18.

slides.title: Read The Psychology of Money.

posts.caption: The easiest habit trick from Atomic Habits. #atomichabits #habits #booktok

slides.title: The one sentence from Atomic Habits that makes new habits stick
"After I [current habit], I will [new habit]."
slides.body: James Clear calls it habit stacking.

slides.title: Why it works
slides.body: Your existing habits are already automatic. Attach the new one and it borrows the cue.

slides.title: Examples
slides.body:
After I pour my coffee, I read 5 pages.

After I sit at my desk, I write my top 3 tasks.

After I brush my teeth, I stretch for 2 minutes.

slides.title: Pick one. Write it down tonight.
